summary: Milestone 2026.04.99 closeout slice took 10 minutes for 2 completed operational items, averaging 5 minutes each. The only nonzero slow path was exp1270 arXiv Bundle v10, which was serially gated on exp1269 critical paper fixes; in-process documentation was effectively zero minutes. Both RTX 3090s were idle at closeout with no GPU processes, so the main efficiency loss was not zombie resource waste but unused parallel capacity and serial gate/docs coupling.

slowest_experiments.name: arXiv Bundle v10 - Gated on Exp 1269 Critical Fixes
slowest_experiments.why_slow: The bundle had a hard dependency on exp1269 completing the five critical paper fixes, then ran TeX compilation and bundle packaging. It was the only measured nonzero item in the supplied timing data.

slowest_experiments.name: In-process docs for arXiv Bundle v10
slowest_experiments.why_slow: Not slow in this slice; it registered as zero minutes. The operational concern is that docs reconciliation remains coupled to the main conductor path instead of being idempotent and async.

bottlenecks_identified: Critical-path serialization: exp1270 could not start until exp1269 had fixed all five paper issues.
GPU capacity sat unused: both RTX 3090s were at 4 MB allocated and 0% utilization at closeout, with no GPU processes.
No material zombie process waste was observed: scripts/gpu_monitor.py --json returned an empty processes list and no warnings.
Pre-flight checks were not the measured bottleneck for this slice: conductor rows around exp1269/exp1270 reported 81 tests passing in 8.24s and 7.89s.
Documentation reconciliation was cheap in the supplied timing, but still runs in the conductor's foreground path and can become serial overhead in larger milestones.
The conductor records only coarse task timing; compile time, gate wait time, docs time, and artifact write time are not separately measured.
Gate-blocked downstream work can still consume conductor cycles unless blocked artifacts are emitted immediately and terminally.
improvements_suggested: Split operational timing into gate_wait_s, preflight_s, execution_s, compile_s, docs_s, artifact_write_s, and reconcile_s for every conductor item.
Run CPU/doc/TeX tasks in parallel with independent GPU experiments whenever gates permit; reserve both GPUs only for tasks that actually need them.
Use DualGPURunner by default for independent Qwen/Gemma or two-model evaluation lanes when GPU tasks are queued.
Cache TeX dependencies and pre-flight state so arXiv bundle reruns pay only the changed-file delta.
Make docs reconciliation idempotent and async, with a foreground fast path that only appends required completion markers.
Emit terminal gate-block artifacts immediately for retired or missing upstream dependencies to avoid retry churn.
Have gpu_monitor.py snapshots attached to experiment artifacts at start and closeout, not only milestone closeout.

gpu_utilization.assessment: GPU utilization was inefficient at the milestone scheduling level: both GPUs were idle, so any independent GPU-capable work could have run concurrently with CPU/doc bundle work. For the two supplied closeout items themselves, no GPU work was required, so the inefficiency is unused scheduling opportunity rather than slow GPU execution.
gpu_utilization.sequential_vs_parallel: No sequential GPU contention was observed because no GPU process was running. The missed opportunity was failing to overlap independent GPU work with CPU-only paper/bundle/doc tasks.

zombie_processes.assessment: No GPU zombie processes were wasting material resources. The 4 MB per GPU baseline allocation was idle residue, below the monitor's zombie threshold and not tied to any compute-app process.

parallelization_opportunities: exp1270 itself was correctly gated on exp1269 and should not have started before the critical paper fixes landed.
The in-process docs pass could have been asynchronous because it did not gate TeX compilation correctness.
Independent GPU experiments in the broader .99 queue could have run while exp1269/exp1270 consumed CPU/docs time.
Downstream tasks with retired upstreams should terminate as structured gate-block artifacts without repeated conductor attempts.

preflight_suite.evidence: Relevant conductor rows reported focused pre-flight checks of 81 passed, 1 warning in 8.24s for exp1269 and 7.89s for exp1270.
preflight_suite.recommendation: Keep the cache-hit focused suite for doc/bundle work; only run broad unit/lint/spec checks when implementation code changes.

doc_reconciliation.assessment: Efficient in this slice because the docs pass registered as 0 minutes, but it should still be made asynchronous and idempotent to avoid becoming a critical-path bottleneck in larger milestones.
doc_reconciliation.recommendation: Batch changelog, roadmap, and status reconciliation after terminal artifacts are written, while still preserving the mandatory skeleton-first artifact behavior.

tooling_infrastructure_changes: Add per-phase conductor timing fields and expose them in ops/metrics.md automatically.
Add a scheduling rule that launches independent GPU work while CPU/doc gates are waiting or compiling.
Attach gpu_monitor.py JSON snapshots to every GPU-capable experiment artifact.
Add an immediate terminal artifact writer for GATE_BLOCK and DOOMED_RERUN_BLOCK outcomes.
Add a TeX bundle cache stamp keyed by main.tex, bibliography, figures, and tectonic cache state.
Add a docs reconciliation append helper that refuses duplicate rows unless the operator explicitly asks for another row.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Instrument conductor phase timing so the next retro can separate gate wait, pre-flight, execution, compile, docs, and artifact costs.
Run independent GPU lanes under DualGPURunner while CPU-only paper, bundle, and docs tasks execute.
Make blocked outcomes and docs reconciliation terminal, idempotent, and fast so the queue does not spend turns on known gate states.

questions_answered.which_experiments_took_longest_and_why: exp1270 took 10 minutes because it sat on the arXiv bundle critical path after exp1269 paper fixes, then compiled and packaged the TeX bundle. The docs pass was 0 minutes.
questions_answered.was_gpu_utilization_efficient: No. Both GPUs were idle at closeout; the slice was CPU/docs-bound, but the scheduler could have overlapped independent GPU work.
questions_answered.were_there_zombie_processes_wasting_reso: No. gpu_monitor.py reported no GPU processes and no warnings.
questions_answered.could_any_experiments_have_been_parallel: exp1270 could not be parallelized with its prerequisite exp1269, but docs reconciliation and independent GPU-capable tasks could have overlapped.
questions_answered.was_preflight_a_bottleneck: No. Focused pre-flight checks were about 8 seconds for exp1269/exp1270 conductor rows.
questions_answered.were_doc_reconciliation_passes_efficient: Yes for this slice, because docs registered 0 minutes; the residual risk is that foreground docs coupling scales poorly.
questions_answered.what_tooling_would_speed_next_milestone: Per-phase timing, DualGPU-aware scheduling, immediate terminal gate-block artifacts, TeX/pre-flight caching, gpu_monitor snapshots per experiment, and idempotent docs append helpers.

meta_reflection: The fastest way to improve the next milestone is to stop treating operational bookkeeping as a single foreground queue. Skeleton-first artifacts are working as loss prevention; the next gain is phase-level timing plus scheduling independent GPU work while CPU/doc critical paths are running.
